speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your double vision, upper limb weakness, and difficulty with stairs, please tell me: do you notice any slurred speech or drooping of your facial muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with eye movement issues, strongly suggests a neuromuscular cause. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies and REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The pattern of weakness worsening with exertion and improving with rest, combined with diplopia that changes with gaze direction, is classic for a neuromuscular junction disorder. The mention of Tuberculosis is inconsistent with your specific symptom profile and should be disregarded. Since you have already mentioned no muscle wasting, we can proceed with a definitive diagnosis based on these clinical findings.
